findings.title: OCR acceptance reports forbidden transcription differences as exact
findings.why_it_matters: The new OCR acceptance mechanism can pass and label a German, English or Russian transcription as exact after the model changes capitalization or punctuation, although RAG-67 grants no such exception. For the committed German ground truth 'Die Seerose blüht auf dem Teich.', the different output 'die seerose blüht auf dem teich?' becomes the same case-folded word array, reaches exact=True and requires no user permission. The printed PDF/DOCX gate uses the same lossy comparison, so a wrong punctuation mark can also pass that gate. Comparing independently transcribed tokens while retaining case and punctuation prevents these differences from silently receiving an undeclared allowance.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the casefold()/\w+ equality used for strict OCR acceptance with case- and punctuation-preserving source tokens or complete independently recorded source strings, allowing only layout whitespace differences explicitly handled by the existing page composition. Use the committed German ground_truth.text and faithful independent EN/RU/printed ground truths; preserve the existing per-word Paddle Belarusian glyph exception and current Qwen Belarusian handwriting exception. Add a small matcher regression proving that a case change and a period-to-question-mark change fail strict acceptance, then rerun the actual OCR integration gates without changing the originals or old raw records.
evidence: backend/tests/integration/test_multilingual_documents.py:230-233 -- exact=row['actual_words']==row['expected_legible_source']; assert exact or exception=='current_Qwen_BE_handwriting',records; row.update({'identity':identity,'acceptance':'exact' if exact else 'user_permitted_current_model_difference', 'exception':exception,'contract':CONTRACT if exception else None})

Constructed sequence: the actual model returns 'die seerose blüht auf dem teich?'; casefold plus \w+ returns ['die','seerose','blüht','auf','dem','teich']; the German be_exception returns None, but exact is True, so the acceptance assertion passes and the evidence record says exact. This is a mechanical guard-fidelity failure, not a claim that the current native run produced this text.
